headline: World leaders gathered for the annual BRICS summit. Here are the takeaways
summary: India hosted the an annual summit which gathered leaders from 28 countries, including the presidents of China and Iran. Though, the U.S. was notably absent.

headline: Can Gulf states and Iran negotiate the Strait of Hormuz without the U.S.?
summary: Dania Thafer of the Gulf International Forum weighs in on previously scheduled talks between Iran and Gulf states. Shortly before this interview aired, Oman announced that the talks were postponed.

headline: Indonesian passenger ship overturns, sparking search for at least 129 missing
summary: Indonesian rescuers said about 130 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people sank in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sunday.

headline: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
summary: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.

headline: 'BRICS' forum brings together emerging economies, aimed at countering western dominance
summary: India hosts the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging markets and developing countries.

headline: Saudi Arabia forced to shut down crucial Red Sea pipeline after attacks
summary: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.

headline: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries
summary: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland

headline: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the BRICS nations for a summit on trade, investment, and global conflicts.

headline: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
summary: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.

headline: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
summary: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.

headline: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
summary: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

headline: The U.S.-Canada trade war is creating a headache for auto-parts makers
summary: For decades, the U.S. and Canadian auto supply chains have been tightly woven together. The trade war is threatening to unravel a complex system.

headline: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
summary: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.

headline: Hong Kong court sentences 3 Tiananmen vigil organizers to prison
summary: The activists were sentenced to about 5 to 7 years in prison in a case widely seen as a barometer of the city's eroding freedoms as Beijing clamps down on dissent.

headline: Iran-backed Houthi rebels seize a strategic port and island, opening a new battlefront
summary: The rebel group took over Yemen's port of Mokha, an area vital to controlling shipping through the Red Sea, Houthi and Yemeni officials said. Mokha is about 50 miles from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

headline: Amid war and sanctions, unemployment worsens in Iran
summary: As the U.S. war with Iran drags on, Iranians face increasing layoffs and a rising unemployment rate.

headline: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
summary: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

headline: UN peacekeepers give NPR a rare look behind Israeli lines
summary: NPR accompanies UN peacekeepers behind Israeli lines as Israel expands its occupation of South Lebanon following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

headline: 'I'll never trust them again': Some Afghans who helped the U.S. post-9/11 regret it
summary: Soon after the Sept. 11 attacks, the U.S. launched what would become a 20-year war in Afghanistan. Some Afghans who helped the U.S. prosecute that war regret it.

headline: After 900 years, the Bayeux Tapestry returns to England and goes on display in London
summary: The nearly 230-foot long Bayeux Tapestry is back in England for the first time in 900 years. It depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings, a turning point in English history that ended Anglo-Saxon rule.

headline: Greetings from Paris, where the 2024 Olympics balloon rises again
summary: The floating Olympic cauldron, held aloft by a giant glowing balloon, is still making regular appearances two years after the 2024 Paris Games, showing up all summer long in the nighttime Paris sky.

headline: U.S. military destroys 5 Iranian oil tankers. And, the Smithsonian head resigns
summary: The U.S. military says it has destroyed five Iranian oil tankers as the conflict continues to escalate. And, Smithsonian head Lonnie G. Bunch III says he plans to step down by the end of the year.

headline: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
summary: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.

headline: Iceland summons U.S. ambassador after Trump posts countries draped with American flag
summary: Iceland summoned the U.S. ambassador after President Trump posted a map on Truth Social that showed the country, along with a number of other nations, covered with an American flag.

headline: U.S. military says it destroyed 5 Iranian oil tankers after attacks on Navy warship
summary: The U.S. military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to the latest attacks on its warships. Iran hit American targets in Jordan.

headline: Kenya's foreign trader crackdown sparks fear among migrant communities
summary: Kenya's president orders a crackdown on foreigners running small businesses, amid accusations of xenophobia.

headline: Australian social media users to be offered choice to opt out of algorithms
summary: A government statement said on Tuesday social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed.

headline: U.K. accuses Israeli settlers of 'ethnic cleansing' in West Bank and bans their goods
summary: France, Canada and other countries joined the U.K. in banning goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israel said it would close the British Consulate among other measures.

headline: GOP to host unusual midterm convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect
summary: Republicans are aiming to get voters to turn out for the midterms with an unconventional convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on the U.S. went into effect at midnight.

headline: Chrystia Freeland negotiated with Trump. Now she's watching a trade war unfold
summary: Chrystia Freeland understands the U.S.-Canada relationship from her time at the negotiating table. Here's what she sees now.

headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia ignite fires at oil facilities and wound 73 people
summary: The attacks come after weeks of escalating clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, which shattered a four-year truce in the country's civil war.

headline: World Food Programme's Carl Skau discusses Yemen's food insecurity crisis
summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Carl Skau of the World Food Programme about the food insecurity crisis in Yemen.

headline: What to know about Canada's escalating trade war with the U.S.
summary: Canada struck back at U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday with tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods. The outcome could resonate far beyond Canada.

headline: King Charles III clarifies status of Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan
summary: King Charles III has reiterated that Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, remain non-working members of the royal family following their return to the United Kingdom.

headline: Russia and North Korea open the first road across their shared border
summary: Relations between Russia and North Korea have been flourishing, with North Korea supplying ammunition and troops to support Russia's war against Ukraine in return for economic and military assistance.

headline: The UN passed resolution ahead of General Assembly calling for end to child marriage
summary: The UN estimates 650 million women and girls currently alive were married before age 18. A new resolution aims to bring awareness and push countries to act to end child marriage.

headline: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting
summary: One week after the deadly floods, very little is known about China's dead or missing. China's control over media and digital censorship is in stark contrast to open reporting in Nepal.

headline: 5 dead after crash at Miami Airport. And, Germany's far-right wins state election
summary: A cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport has left five people dead and several others injured. And, Germany's far-right AfD party achieves an electoral victory in a key state election.

headline: Kushner and Witkoff visit Ukraine with hopes of restarting peace talks with Russia
summary: For the first time, Trump's top envoys take their peace push to Kyiv — after talks with Putin in Moscow.

headline: Former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine on efforts to strike a compromise with Russia
summary: NPR's Leila Fadel asks William Taylor, former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, about efforts made by U.S. emissaries toward a compromise between Russia and Ukraine.

headline: Rubio to visit 3 Latin American countries this week
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Colombia, Peru and Ecuador as President Trump hails a shift to the right in regional politics and a new era of U.S. dominance.

headline: U.S. envoys visit Kyiv for first time after meeting Putin in Moscow
summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff made their first trip to Kyiv, one day after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

headline: Shipping companies are putting sails back on cargo ships
summary: One of the world's largest logistics companies plans to fit one of its ships with a strange type of sail, the latest in a small but growing number of cleaner sailing shipping vessels.

headline: What Russia and China learned from America after 9/11
summary: Journalists Mikhail Zygar and Cindy Yu explain how the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan helped reshape Russia and China's ambitions.

headline: Germany's far-right achieves an electoral breakthrough in key state election
summary: Germany's populist, far-right Alternative for Germany party has declared victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt after more than doubling its share of the vote in the first of several regional elections this fall.

headline: German exit polls suggest far-right party has big lead in regional election
summary: Exit polls show Germany's AfD taking a commanding lead in a regional election, but it remains unclear whether the far-right party can form the country's first state government since World War II.

headline: Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after Moscow Putin meeting
summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held meetings in Kyiv with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy on Sunday, a day after lengthy conversations with Russian President Putin in Moscow.

headline: U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers in renewal of hostilities
summary: The U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets two American warships, in the latest exchange over shipping and the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: This is the work of our lifetime: Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges action after new UN climate report
summary: A United Nations report has found that the world will warm to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Climate solutions advocate Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges a quicker implementation of known strategies - and determination rather than despair.

headline: U.S. and Iran trade attacks on ships as fighting flares up again
How the U.S. focus on Iran is fueling a more aggressive Putin
summary: Trump's top envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv as Putin steps up round the clock bombing of Ukraine. With the U.S. distracted by Iran, is Putin becoming increasingly emboldened?

headline: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal puts opposition in a political bind
summary: Venezuelan opposition members are uneasy with new oil deals with the U.S., worried that agreements with authoritarian regime in Caracas could undermine democratic progress.

headline: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.

headline: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest
summary: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte has posted bail after order issued for her arrest on charges she publicly threatened to arrange assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two others.

headline: The U.N. backs a new world map showing Africa in its true relative size
summary: The U.N. has backed a new map showing Africa in its true relative size, with the U.S. standing alone in opposition.

headline: Philippine vice president is ordered arrested for threats against the president
summary: It's part of a political showdown with Marcos. A trial could impact her plans to run for president in 2028.

headline: Myanmar military head visits Vietnam to normalize relations
summary: His trip to Vietnam marks his third visit to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore Myanmar's standing in the bloc.

headline: Trump asks SCOTUS to OK changes to mail-in ballots. And, diesel prices hit record high
summary: Trump has asked the Supreme Court to lift the block on his plan for the USPS to restrict mail voting ahead of the midterm elections. And, diesel prices have reached a record high.

headline: Germany's far-right AfD party is poised for power in a state election
summary: Germany's AfD's TikTok-fueled rise in Saxony-Anhalt is raising fears the country could see its first far-right governor since World War II.

headline: Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine's capital
summary: In Ukraine, a week of near-continuous Russian attacks is upending the lives of residents in Kyiv and its suburbs.

headline: Argentina escalates Falklands dispute with the U.K., seizing on Trump comments
summary: Argentine President Javier Milei is escalating a dispute with Britain over the Falkland Islands with tougher sanctions targeting companies involved in a major offshore oil project.
